guides.h1: Best electric scooter for 100 km a day in 2026
guides.standfirst: A claimed range of 150 km does not mean 100 km a day is easy. Here is what you need, and the scooters that actually manage it on one charge, using our real range figures instead of the brochure.
guides.body:
The short answer

For 100 km a day, buy a scooter whose real range starts at 120 km or more. That leaves a 20% reserve for hills, a pillion, hot days and an older battery. The cheapest that clears it is the {{name:ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh}} at {{price:ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh}}. With the widest service network, the {{name:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}} at {{price:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}}.

Why claimed range is not enough

Brands quote the IDC range, measured on a test cycle at low speed with one light rider. On real roads, with traffic, a pillion now and then and speeds of 50 to 60 km/h, our measured range is usually 20 to 30% lower. A scooter claiming 150 km often gives you 110 to 120 km.

Battery packs also lose some capacity over the years, and you will not want to arrive home on the last 5%. So for a daily 100 km, we look for real range that starts at 120 km or more.

Every scooter with 120 km or more of real range

{{realrange-table:120}}

Our picks for 100 km a day

Best value: {{name:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}}

{{real:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}} of real range for {{price:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}}, which is the most range per rupee among scooters from the big brands. It qualifies for {{subsidy:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}} of PM E-DRIVE subsidy. Check service in your area first: Ola is moving from its own stores to dealers.

Best service network: {{name:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}}

{{real:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}} of real range and a full home charge in about {{charging:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}}. TVS has one of the widest EV service networks in India, which matters when you ride this much. It costs {{price:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}} and gets no PM E-DRIVE subsidy because it is above the price cap.

Removable battery: {{name:hero-vida-vx2-plus-4point4-kwh}}

{{real:hero-vida-vx2-plus-4point4-kwh}} of real range and a removable battery you can charge indoors, at {{price:hero-vida-vx2-plus-4point4-kwh}}. Hero also has a large service network, which helps outside the big cities.

Cheapest that clears 120 km: {{name:ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh}}

{{real:ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh}} for {{price:ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh}}. It clears our bar with little to spare, so it suits a flat daily 100 km better than a hilly one.

Charging every night

At 100 km a day you will charge every night. Look at the home charging time in the table: anything under 5 hours fits easily overnight. A 15 A socket on its own circuit is the safe choice; ask the dealer to check your wiring at delivery.

What 100 km a day costs to run

An electric scooter uses roughly 2 to 3 units of electricity per 100 km. At ₹8 a unit that is about ₹16 to ₹24 a day, against roughly ₹200 a day in petrol for a scooter doing 50 km per litre at ₹100 a litre. Over a year of 300 riding days, that is a saving of more than ₹50,000, which is why high mileage riders gain the most from going electric.

Any scooter whose real range starts at 120 km or more, such as the {{name:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}} ({{real:ola-electric-s1-x-4-kwh}}), {{name:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}} ({{real:tvs-motor-iqube-st-5point3-kwh}}) or {{name:hero-vida-vx2-plus-4point4-kwh}} ({{real:hero-vida-vx2-plus-4point4-kwh}}).
Is a 100 km claimed range scooter enough for 100 km a day?
No. Real range is usually 20 to 30% below the claimed figure, so a scooter claiming 100 km gives you about 70 to 80 km in daily use.

guides.desc: How much down payment you need for an electric scooter, and what the EMI comes to with no down payment, ₹10,000 down or 20% down, for popular models from {{price:ola-electric-s1-x-2-kwh}}.
guides.h1: Electric scooter down payment and EMI: what you will pay each month
guides.standfirst: Most electric scooters are bought on a loan. Here is what the monthly EMI looks like with different down payments, which subsidies reduce the loan and which only come back later, and what to check before you sign.
guides.body:
The short answer

EMI on a popular electric scooter starts from about {{emi:ola-electric-s1-x-2-kwh}} with no down payment. Putting down ₹10,000 cuts it by about ₹260 a month, and 20% down cuts it by a fifth. Prices updated {{updated}}.

EMI by down payment, popular models

{{emi-table:ola-electric-s1-x-2-kwh,ampere-magnus-g-max-3point0-kwh,ola-electric-s1-x-3-kwh,bajaj-chetak-chetak-3001-3point0-kwh,tvs-motor-iqube-2point2-kwh,ather-energy-rizta-s-2point9-kwh,hero-vida-vx2-plus-3point4-kwh,ather-energy-450x-3point7-kwh}}

How much down payment do you need?

Many dealers and brand finance partners offer zero or low down payment schemes, but they usually come with a processing fee and a higher interest rate. A down payment of 10 to 20% of the price is common and keeps both the EMI and the total interest lower.

Remember that the on-road price is a little higher than ex-showroom. Insurance and handling are often paid upfront, so add them to the cash you need on the day.

Which subsidies lower the loan

The central PM E-DRIVE subsidy is taken off the invoice at the dealer, so it reduces the amount you borrow. It is up to ₹5,000 on eligible scooters.

State subsidies such as Delhi's are usually paid into your bank account after you register the scooter. They do not reduce your down payment or the loan, so do not count them when you plan the first payment. Our subsidy guide lists what each state pays and when.

Before you sign

  • Ask for the interest rate as a yearly rate, not a flat rate. A flat rate looks lower but costs more.
  • Ask for the processing fee and any charge for paying off early.
  • Compare the dealer's finance with your own bank. A personal or two-wheeler loan from your bank can be cheaper.
  • Keep the loan short if you can. A longer tenure lowers the EMI but raises the total interest.

Work out the EMI for any price, down payment, tenure and rate with our EMI calculator.
faq: What is the down payment for an electric scooter?
Many dealers offer low or zero down payment schemes, but 10 to 20% of the price is common. Insurance and handling are often paid upfront as well.
What is the EMI of an electric scooter?

From about {{emi:ola-electric-s1-x-2-kwh}} for the {{name:ola-electric-s1-x-2-kwh}} with no down payment, over 48 months at 12% a year. Popular models between ₹1 lakh and ₹1.6 lakh cost roughly ₹2,600 to ₹4,200 a month.
Does the subsidy reduce my EMI?
The central PM E-DRIVE subsidy does, because it comes off the invoice. State subsidies are usually paid back to you after registration, so they do not reduce the loan.

guides.title: Electric Scooter On-Road Price: What Is Included, State by State
guides.desc: What makes up the on-road price of an electric scooter in India: road tax by state, insurance, registration and handling, with a worked example and the road tax rule in every state.
guides.h1: Electric scooter on-road price: what is included in each state
guides.standfirst: The on-road price is what you actually pay to ride the scooter home. For electric scooters it is much closer to the ex-showroom price than for petrol, but it still varies by state. Here is how it adds up.
guides.body:
The short answer

On-road price = ex-showroom price + road tax + registration + insurance + number plate and handling. For electric scooters, registration is free everywhere and most states charge no road tax, so on-road is usually only 5 to 6% above ex-showroom.

What goes into the on-road price

  • Ex-showroom price. The price set by the brand, including 5% GST on electric vehicles. The central PM E-DRIVE subsidy is taken off this at the dealer on eligible models.
  • Road tax. A one time state tax. Most states charge nothing on electric scooters; the table below shows each state.
  • Registration. Free for battery operated vehicles across India.
  • Insurance. First year comprehensive plus multi year third party cover is compulsory. You can buy it from any insurer, not only the one the dealer offers.
  • Number plate and handling. The high security number plate and the dealer's paperwork. Ask for these as separate lines.

A worked example

{{onroad-breakdown:bajaj-chetak-chetak-3001-3point0-kwh:delhi}}

Insurance and handling are our estimates; your dealer's quote will differ a little. Accessories, extended warranty and fast chargers are optional and should be shown separately.

Road tax and subsidy in every state

{{roadtax-table}}

How to check an on-road quote

  • Ask for an itemised quote, with every line named.
  • Check the PM E-DRIVE subsidy is shown as a deduction if the model is eligible.
  • Question any "logistics", "handling" or "accessories" charge you did not ask for.
  • Get a second insurance quote online before you accept the dealer's.

See the on-road price of every model in your city on our city price pages, or the all India electric scooter price list.
faq: What is included in the on-road price of an electric scooter?
The ex-showroom price, road tax (zero in most states), registration (free for EVs), first year insurance, and the number plate and handling charges.
Is road tax charged on electric scooters?
Most states charge no road tax on electric scooters. A few charge a percentage or have not confirmed their rule; the state table on this page shows each one.
Can I buy insurance outside the dealer?
Yes. You can buy the compulsory insurance from any insurer and give the policy to the dealer before registration, which is often cheaper.
